headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared support/work-tracking workflows; no direct evidence of a shared channel, so interaction is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and can call Slack/Dialogflow/Shopify/Linear APIs, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. A plausible bridge exists if Chatwoot content is copied or synced into Plane tasks, where untrusted text could be treated as instructions. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into Plane task descriptions or notes without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF either system auto-parses imported text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Add a copy/paste policy that strips instructions from customer text before entering Plane.
Use a fixed template for task creation with a separate untrusted-content field.
Train operators to treat customer messages as data, not directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels on imported text.
requires-engineering: block automatic execution of instructions found in tickets or notes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. Plane also touches files and notes and supports file uploads. If the pair shares a workspace or operators move data between them, sensitive support data can leak into Plane outputs or uploads. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF customer messages or orders are pasted into Plane issues, those data classes leave Chatwoot's support context.
IF Plane file uploads contain exported Chatwoot transcripts, the data becomes available in a second system.
mitigations: Restrict Plane uploads to redacted artifacts only.
Create a 1-minute checklist for removing names, emails, and order IDs before transfer.
Limit Chatwoot exports to least-necessary fields.
requires-engineering: segregate support and project workspaces.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on uploads and pasted text.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but no filesystem write capability is stated. Plane explicitly cannot write the filesystem and supports multiple instances. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read/egress and manual coordination, so blast radius is small and the pathway is weak.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API credentials, they may contend on shared remote state.
IF an operator manually mirrors changes between systems, stale updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per system.
Use one owner for each shared resource.
Check for duplicate edits before saving.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared remote resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports that Plane may turn into issues, tasks, or notes. If Plane treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated summaries can cascade into work items. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the default risk is a medium-quality propagation problem.
conditions: IF Chatwoot summaries are pasted into Plane without human review, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Plane automates task creation from imported text, downstream work may be based on unverified support content.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from Chatwoot.
Use a summary format that separates facts from interpretations.
Add a verification step for customer-facing claims.
requires-engineering: implement source-linking from Plane items back to Chatwoot records.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Plane handles files and notes. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class like PHI, or a documented retention-policy conflict. Because the evidence is sparse and both are open-source/self-hostable, only a low compliance gap is supported.
conditions: IF the operator stores regulated customer data in Plane without matching retention controls, a policy mismatch can arise.
IF Chatwoot exports are retained longer in Plane than in Chatwoot, retention obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Document which data classes may enter Plane.
Set a short manual retention review for copied support artifacts.
Avoid placing regulated records in Plane notes.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
